newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Borsodchem reports rising export in Q1 '97.
newsitem.headline: Borsodchem reports rising export in Q1 '97.

text.p: Hungarian chemicals firm Borsodchem said on Wednesday its exports accounted for an increasing part of its sales which rose 31.9 percent in the first quarter of 1997 over the same period of 1996.
"Within sales revenues exports continued to account for a higher proportion," Borsodchem said in its earnings report.

"Exports accounted for 67.3 percent of total sales as export revenues rose by 2.913 billion forints or 46.9 percent from the base period." In the first quarter of 1996 exports accounted for 60.5 percent.
Borsodchem released its consolidated HAS earnings report for January-March 1997 this morning and said its sales revenues rose to 13.557 billion forints from 10.276 billion.
Its operating profit rose 10.7 percent to 1.941 billion forints from 1.753 billion, while its after-tax profit rose 3.9 percent to 1.758 billion from 1.693 billion.

Borsodchem attributed the rise in its sales revenues mainly to a 57.9 percent increase in PVC powder prices in the first quarter of 1997 over the first three months of 1996, triggered by higher sales prices and higher volumes.
It added that revenues from MDI (methylene diphenyl diisocyanate) products, semi-finished and finished plastics products also grew "substantially."
In volume terms Borsodchem's sales of PVC powder rose 10.3 percent while MDI increased 20.1 percent, it said.
Revenues from caustic soda and compaunds decreased due to lower world market prices and lower demand, respectively. -- Emese Bartha, Budapest newsroom +36 1 327-4040
